I'm a PhD student in ecology at the **University of Oxford**, working on the
ecological credibility and long-term durability of biodiversity and
nature-based carbon offsets — when offsets actually deliver the outcomes they
claim, and what the answer means for conservation policy and finance.

This site collects analysis walkthroughs from my project repositories, shorter
blog-style notes, and a handful of interactive tools.

## Research interests
- Biodiversity and nature-based offsets
- Permanence, additionality, and leakage
- Conservation finance and policy
- Reproducible ecological data analysis

## Currently
Working on a structured review of permanence risks across biodiversity and
nature-based carbon offset schemes — see the
[walkthrough](walkthroughs/offset-permanence/index.qmd) and the
[project repository](https://github.com/alexdhond/offset-permanence-review).
